questions.context:
When the small fishing village of Porto Azul lost its only school five years ago, everyone thought the village would slowly die. Young families moved away, and the old houses stood empty. Then two teachers, Clara and Miguel Santos, arrived with a strange idea: a school without classrooms.

Their school uses the whole village. Mathematics happens in the market, where children weigh fruit and count change. Biology takes place on the boats with the fishermen. History is taught by the oldest villagers, who tell stories of storms and celebrations. Art is painted on walls that were once grey.

At first, only six children joined. But the idea spread. Today, forty-two students come from villages all around the region, travelling by minibus every morning. The fishermen, who once worried about noisy children, now fight to take them out to sea. 'They are our future,' says one.

The village has changed too. Three empty houses became a bakery, a small hotel and a bookshop. 'A school is not a building,' Clara says. 'It is the heart of a place. When the heart beats, everything wakes up.'
questions.stem: What problem did Porto Azul have five years ago?
questions.explanation: The village lost its only school and families moved away.

tasks.title: Mock 6 · Part 1: Reply to Sam's email
tasks.rubric: Read the email from your English friend Sam. Write a reply answering all four points (about 100 words).
tasks.inputText:
Hi!
Thanks for your last email — your photos from the trip looked amazing!
I've got news: I'm going to learn to cook this summer. Can you give me some advice for a beginner? What's the easiest dish to start with?
Also, my family wants to eat more healthily. Do you know any easy healthy recipes?
And finally — would you like to cook something together when we meet in August? We could try a new recipe!
Speak soon!
Sam
points: Give advice for a beginner cook
Answer about cooking together in August
tasks.model:
Hi Sam,

Great idea — cooking is a skill for life!

My advice for beginners: start with simple recipes and always read them completely before you begin. Don't worry about mistakes — everyone makes them!

The easiest first dish is pasta with tomato sauce. You need only five ingredients, and it's almost impossible to make badly.

For something healthy, try a big salad with chicken, nuts and fruit. It's quick, colourful, and your family will love it.

And yes — I'd love to cook together in August! Let's try a pizza recipe from zero. I'll bring the flour!

Speak soon,
Diego
tasks.modelNotes: Advice, a dish, a healthy idea and an enthusiastic answer — all four points in order.
checklist: All four content points are answered
The closing is warm and concrete

tasks.title: Mock 6 · Part 2: The best present I ever received
tasks.rubric: A magazine asks readers to write articles about presents. Write your article about the best present you ever received (about 100 words), saying what it was, who gave it to you, and why it was special.
points: Say who gave it to you
tasks.model:
The Best Present I Ever Received

What is the best present you have ever received? An expensive phone? A new bike? Mine cost almost nothing — and it's the most valuable thing I own.

When I was ten, my grandfather gave me his old camera. It was heavy, silver, and older than my parents! 'This camera saw the world,' he said. 'Now show me yours.'

That summer, I photographed everything: my dog, the market, rain on the window. My grandfather taught me to look slowly and carefully.

He died two years later, but the camera is still with me. Every photo I take connects us. All in all, he didn't give me a camera — he gave me a way of seeing.

l_m6_p3_main.speaker: W
l_m6_p3_main.text: Welcome, everyone, to today's talk about the Millbrook Farm Shop. I'm David, the owner's son, and I'll tell you our story.

l_m6_p3_main.speaker: W
l_m6_p3_main.text: Millbrook Farm Shop opened fifteen years ago in an old barn. We are open every day except Christmas, from nine in the morning until half past five in the afternoon.

l_m6_p3_main.speaker: W
l_m6_p3_main.text: Everything we sell comes from our own farm or from farms within twenty kilometres. You can buy our cheese, honey, and bread — and the most popular product of all, our apple juice, made from six kinds of apples.

l_m6_p3_main.speaker: W
l_m6_p3_main.text: Families love our Saturday mornings: children can feed the animals at eleven o'clock, and there is a free farm tour at two in the afternoon.

l_m6_p3_main.speaker: W
l_m6_p3_main.text: You'll find us on Millbrook Lane, three kilometres north of the town centre. Follow the brown signs from the main road. We hope to see you soon!

l_m6_p4_main.speaker: M
l_m6_p4_main.text: My guest today turned a hobby into a business before she was eighteen. Welcome, Rosa Martins — founder of 'Bags from Banners'.

l_m6_p4_main.speaker: W2
l_m6_p4_main.text: Thanks for inviting me! Yes, I make bags and pencil cases out of old festival banners — the big colourful ones you see at concerts.

l_m6_p4_main.speaker: W2
l_m6_p4_main.text: My mother works for a company that organises festivals. Two years ago, she told me they throw away hundreds of banners every year. I thought that was crazy — they're beautiful and strong! So I took some home and made a bag for school. My classmates all wanted one.

l_m6_p4_main.speaker: W2
l_m6_p4_main.text: I started selling them online. Each bag is unique because every banner is different. Last year I sold over four hundred bags, and I donated ten percent of the money to an environmental charity.

l_m6_p4_main.speaker: M
l_m6_p4_main.text: Is it difficult to run a business while studying?

l_m6_p4_main.speaker: W2
l_m6_p4_main.text: It takes organisation! I make bags at weekends and post them on Mondays. My school supports me — my economics teacher even uses my business as an example in class!

l_m6_p4_main.speaker: W2
l_m6_p4_main.text: I'm designing a line of beach bags for summer. And my dream? A workshop where other young people can learn to make things from waste. Throwing away is easy — creating is better.
